# Image encoders

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">HGGD only</span><code class="gp-chip">--set image_encoder=</code><span class="gp-chip">38 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

An image encoder turns the colour image, or colour and depth, into feature maps. HGGD predicts
its grasp heat-map from them; the seed-based methods can read them only through point painting,
below.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

```bash
grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e \
    --set image_encoder=resnet34 -o hggd_resnet34.yaml
grasppanda compose hggd/hggd_r34w8_g1b-realsense_15e --list image_encoder
```

HGGD is the one method with this slot. The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [HGGD](../methods/hggd.md#image-encoder).

<!-- method-options:end -->

One option of a preset changes on the same line, for example
`--opts model.image_encoder.depth=depth_stem model.image_encoder.frozen=true`.

??? note "What the columns say, and who is left out"

    - **Runs**: out of the methods the option is a swap under, those under which its probe trained on real frames without error. A method that ships the option is named *own* and not counted; a method still undecided is counted and named. Measured on 20 training iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, one run per cell; nothing was measured on GraspClutter6D or on Kinect frames.
    - **Trains like shipped**: out of the methods under which the swap ran, those under which every comparable loss term ended within the method's tolerance of the component it ships, with nothing rising; a method left out is named with why. Measured on 250 iterations on 8 RealSense frames of GraspNet-1Billion (one scene), seed 0, at a constant learning rate (FineGrasp: its own warm-up), beside the method as shipped trained the same way twice.
    - [How we measure](../evidence/index.md) defines every word of these columns.

## Choosing

- **Depth or not.** `depth: rgb_only` uses pretrained features as released;
  `fourth_channel` suits convolutional pyramids you fine-tune; `depth_stem` suits a frozen
  encoder.
- **Freeze foundation models** (DINOv2 and v3, SigLIP 2, RADIO) on small data:
  `frozen: true`.
- **Any stride fits.** A pyramid decoder takes maps of any strides and widths; only
  `hggd-residual` keeps HGGD's own decoder, so its checkpoints load.
- **Weights download on first use** and print their licence. A preset never switches
  non-commercial weights on, and an encoder that runs code from its hub repository needs
  `accept_remote_code: true`.
- **The seed-based methods** read an image through point painting, which you write into a
  config by hand.

## Point painting {#point-painting}

<!-- slot-reach:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

<span class="gp-chip gp-chip--muted" title="point painting: a wrapper written into a config by hand (compose does not write it); no probe record">no record</span> `image-painted`, `image-painted-subsampled` · point painting: a wrapper written into a config by hand (compose does not write it); no probe record.

<!-- slot-reach:end -->

`ImagePainted` (around a dense scene encoder) and `ImagePaintedSubsampled` (around a
sub-sampling one) project every point into the colour image and give the 3-D network the image
features at its pixel, as extra input channels (`fusion: input`) or as a residual on its output
(`fusion: output`). A painted config also changes the dataset node of every split, so compose
does not write it: start from the presets `image-painted` and `image-painted-subsampled` and the
fragment below.

??? note "The complete fragment, for GraspNet-baseline and GSNet"

    A file next to the shipped configs, for example `configs/experimental/my_painted.yaml`.
    GraspNet-baseline has a sub-sampling encoder, so it takes `ImagePaintedSubsampled`; GSNet
    has a dense one and takes `ImagePainted`.

    === "GraspNet-baseline"

        ```yaml
        _base_:
          - ../graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e.yaml

        model:
          backbone:
            _delete_: true                  # replace the base config's encoder node
            type: ImagePaintedSubsampled    # around a sub-sampling encoder
            fusion: input                   # input | output
            paint_channels: 32
            image_scale: 0.5                # encode 640 x 360 instead of the 1280 x 720 sensor image
            image_encoder:                  # any image-encoder node with depth: rgb_only
              type: TimmImageEncoder
              name: resnet18.a1_in1k
              pretrained: true
              out_indices: [1, 2]           # strides 4 and 8
              depth: rgb_only
            backbone:
              type: PointNet2               # the encoder of GraspNet-baseline
              in_channels: 32               # 0 point features + 32 painted channels
              npoints: [2048, 1024, 512, 256]
              radii: [0.04, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3]
              nsamples: [64, 32, 16, 16]
              fps_skip_near_origin: true
              fps_tie_break: pointnet2_cuda

        data:
          train:
            dataset:
              images: [rgb]
              transforms:                   # the base list without RandomFlip and RandomRotation
                - {type: RandomSample, num_points: 20000}
                - {type: FilterObjects, min_visible_points: 50, exclude_object_ids: [18]}
                - {type: SampleGraspLabels, point_fraction: 0.25, min_points: 300, collision: zero_scores, visible_within: 0.01, grids: deferred}
          val: {dataset: {images: [rgb]}}
          test: {dataset: {images: [rgb]}}
        ```

    === "GSNet"

        ```yaml
        _base_:
          - ../gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e.yaml

        model:
          backbone:
            _delete_: true                  # replace the base config's encoder node
            type: ImagePainted              # around a dense encoder
            fusion: input                   # input | output
            paint_channels: 32
            image_scale: 0.5                # encode 640 x 360 instead of the 1280 x 720 sensor image
            image_encoder:                  # any image-encoder node with depth: rgb_only
              type: TimmImageEncoder
              name: resnet18.a1_in1k
              pretrained: true
              out_indices: [1, 2]           # strides 4 and 8
              depth: rgb_only
            backbone:
              type: SparseUNet14            # the encoder of GSNet
              in_channels: 35               # 3 constant ones + 32 painted channels
              out_channels: 512
              voxel_size: 0.005

        data:
          train:
            dataset:
              images: [rgb]
              transforms:                   # the base list without RandomFlip and RandomRotation
                - {type: RandomSample, num_points: 15000}
                - {type: FilterObjects, min_visible_points: 50}
                - {type: SampleGraspLabels, point_fraction: 0.25, min_points: 300, collision: zero_scores, grids: deferred}
                - {type: ConstantFeatures, channels: 3}
          val: {dataset: {images: [rgb]}}
          test: {dataset: {images: [rgb]}}
        ```

    Under every seed-based detector type, the wrapper of the kind its proposal needs builds and
    asks for the colour image (`tests/unit/test_all_methods_skeleton.py`). For another
    seed-based method, inherit its config and wrap its own encoder:
    `ImagePaintedSubsampled` around the sub-sampling encoder of Scale-Balanced-Grasp,
    `ImagePainted` around the dense ones of EconomicGrasp and FineGrasp. With `fusion: input`
    the wrapped encoder's `in_channels` is what the detector feeds plus `paint_channels`; with
    `fusion: output` it stays as it was. A painted FineGrasp config needs
    `images: [depth, rgb]`, because FineGrasp already reads the depth image for its normals.

??? note "What the data pipeline delivers, and what it does not"

    - `images: [rgb]` puts the colour image into `observation.rgb`; the camera matrix is always
      there and points are in the camera frame, so the pixel of a point is its projection. A
      scene encoder that declares `uses_observation = True` is called with the observation.
    - **No painting under point augmentation.** A dataset that serves images refuses
      `RandomFlip` and `RandomRotation`, because a moved cloud no longer projects onto its
      image. Carrying the per-point pixel index into the batch would lift this; it changes the
      data contract of every method and is not done.
    - **No probe record.** The grid composes its cells, and compose does not write painted
      configs, so no verdict is shown here. One painted config per seed-based method was probed
      by hand while the wrappers were built; those runs are not records and cannot be reproduced
      from the repository.

## Details

??? note "Input and output"

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | input | `image`: `(B, in_channels, H, W)`, float, upright |
    | `input_layout` | `rgb`: colour in [0, 1], normalised by the encoder for its weights; `rgbd`: the same followed by depth in metres; `drgb`: HGGD's own order, the reference encoder only |
    | output | a list of `(B, out_channels[i], h_i, w_i)` maps, finest first |
    | `out_strides`, `out_channels` | stride and width of every map; the bridges measure them with one forward pass when built |

    HGGD hands over a transposed `[depth, R, G, B]` image. For any encoder but its own, HGGD turns
    it upright, re-orders the channels to the encoder's layout and turns the maps back; a pyramid
    decoder projects every map to `model.encoder.decoder_channels`, merges them and resamples to
    the stride of HGGD's proposals. The reference encoder keeps the reference decoder, so the
    model is the one of the shipped config and converted checkpoints load.

    `image_encoder` is a typed slot: a node is checked against the constructor of its class
    before anything is built.

??? note "RGB-D: what each depth mode does"

    No library ships weights pretrained on RGB-D, and timm's `in_chans=4` only repeats the colour
    filters. So depth is an explicit option of every bridge:

    | `depth` | What the encoder sees | Pretrained weights |
    |---|---|---|
    | `rgb_only` (default of the presets) | colour, 3 channels | used as released; depth still reaches HGGD's region stage as points |
    | `fourth_channel` | colour + depth; the first convolution (or patch embedding) gets a fourth input | colour filters as released; the depth filters start at zero (or at the mean colour filter) and always train |
    | `depth_stem` | colour + a residual computed from depth by a small stem of its own | untouched; with `frozen: true` only the stem and the decoder learn |

??? note "The settings that matter"

    | Setting | How to choose |
    |---|---|
    | `depth` | `rgb_only` to use pretrained features as they are; `fourth_channel` for convolutional pyramids you fine-tune; `depth_stem` when the encoder is frozen |
    | `frozen` | `true` for foundation ViTs and small data; batch-norm statistics stay fixed too |
    | `out_indices` (timm, transformers) | which levels come out; for ViTs `[3, 6, 9, 12]` gives the decoder four depths to merge |
    | `input_size` | for models of one fixed size (MaxViT, Hiera, EVA-02, timm's DINOv2 and SigLIP): the image is resampled to it |
    | `size_multiple` | for models that take any multiple of their patch or window: the image is resampled up to it |
    | `model_args` | free-form arguments of the library (`drop_path_rate`, `window_size`, `trust_remote_code`) |
    | `model.encoder.decoder_channels` | 64 by default; wider helps a wide encoder and costs memory in the region stage |
    | `model.encoder.detach_features` | `true` (the reference recipe): the region loss does not train the image network |

    The bridges expose far more than the presets: `TimmImageEncoder(name=<any timm model with
    features_only>)`, `HFImageEncoder(name=<hub id or local directory>)`,
    `TorchvisionImageEncoder(name=<resnet*, regnet*, or a model with .features>)`.

??? note "Weights and their licences"

    timm and transformers download a preset's weights on first use (`HF_HOME` chooses the
    cache) and print one line with the name and the licence the library states; a local file is
    `checkpoint:`. Non-commercial weights are supported, never switched on by a preset: such a
    preset sets `pretrained: false`.

    | Option | Weights and their licence |
    |---|---|
    | `hggd-residual` | none released for the encoder alone; the authors' HGGD checkpoints convert with `tools/convert_checkpoint.py` and load into this model. |
    | `resnet18` | `resnet18.a1_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `resnet34` | `resnet34.a1_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `resnet34-rgbd` | `resnet34.a1_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `resnet50` | `resnet50.a1_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `convnextv2-tiny` | `convnextv2_tiny.fcmae_ft_in22k_in1k`, CC BY-NC 4.0: NON-COMMERCIAL weights, **off in the preset** (`pretrained: false`; `--opts model.image_encoder.pretrained=true` fetches them). |
    | `convnextv2-atto` | `convnextv2_atto.fcmae_ft_in1k`, CC BY-NC 4.0: NON-COMMERCIAL weights, **off in the preset** (`pretrained: false`; `--opts model.image_encoder.pretrained=true` fetches them). |
    | `efficientnetv2-s` | `tf_efficientnetv2_s.in21k_ft_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `mobilenetv4-conv-small` | `mobilenetv4_conv_small.e2400_r224_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `mobilenetv4-hybrid-medium` | `mobilenetv4_hybrid_medium.e500_r224_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `repvit-m1` | `repvit_m1.dist_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |
    | `fastvit-sa12` | `fastvit_sa12.apple_in1k`, Apple's FastViT licence (timm: `fastvit-license`; read it before any use beyond research). |
    | `fastvit-t8` | `fastvit_t8.apple_in1k`, Apple's FastViT licence (timm: `fastvit-license`). |
    | `efficientvit-b1` | `efficientvit_b1.r224_in1k`, Apache-2.0 (timm). |

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **HGGD's image is transposed.** A pretrained network fed it sees a mirrored, rotated
      picture, so HGGD turns the image upright for every encoder but its own.
    - **Fixed-size transformers** (timm's DINOv2, EVA-02, SigLIP, MaxViT, Hiera) assert the image
      size they were built for; `input_size` and `size_multiple` resample, and the presets carry
      values that ran.
    - **Swin V2 in timm** needs every stage to be a multiple of its window; the transformers
      version pads by itself.
    - **Hiera's MAE checkpoints** have positions for 224 × 224 only; `hf-hiera-tiny` squeezes the
      image to that square, `hiera-small-abswin` and `sam2-hiera-tiny` take it at its size.
    - **Channels-last maps** of timm's Swin cannot be told apart by shape; the bridge reads timm's
      declared output format.
    - **Depth Anything V2** is a depth-estimation model on the hub: `api: depth_backbone` takes
      its DINOv2 encoder out.
    - **Meta's own DINOv3 repositories are gated**; timm's mirrors are not and are what the
      presets use.
    - **A nested encoder node gets its defaults filled in by the config loader**, so a wrapper
      cannot inject `in_channels` into the encoder it wraps; the painted wrappers read it from the
      wrapped node instead.

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | MambaVision | its hub code needs `mamba_ssm`, a compiled CUDA extension; its weights are non-commercial. |
    | Meta's gated DINOv3 repositories | `HFImageEncoder` loads them once you have access; the presets use timm's mirrors. |
    | timm's MAE Hiera | cannot be built for another image size; use `hiera-small-abswin`. |
    | RGB-D fusion encoders (CMX, CMNeXt, TokenFusion, DFormer) | two streams fused at every stage: not one library model behind `forward(image)`; the contract `input_layout: rgbd` is ready for one. |
    | torchvision's transformers | `TorchvisionImageEncoder` cuts chains of stages only; timm has the same architectures. |
    | Image features at every level of the 3-D decoder (as DITR does) | needs the wrapped encoder to expose its levels; input and output fusion are offered. |
